Tablet of the Kings:
We who served the last king set this stone apart from its brothers, so that the gate stays shut. Under Teku-Sul the roots of every Hist meet, and the Eye sits where they meet and binds them. Set your hand to it where it sits, and strength runs down every root to every tree. Lift it from its place, and every tree is cut from every other, for good, and the weak among them die alone. The king would not trust either act to any one hand. So we sealed it.

content.text:
I took the second seal-stone from the drowned vaults of Gemin, which completes "The Vault's Stone". Nobody there would talk to me, so I never had to fight or sneak past the Warden, the Unbound Rearguard or the Restless Dead.

I now hold two of the three stones (Blackrose Prison and Gemin) and the Warden Vault Key.

The Tablet of the Kings says the Eye at the Root strengthens every Hist tree if I use it where it sits. If I lift it from its place, it cuts every tree off from the others and the weak ones die alone. So I must use the Eye in place and never lift it.

The Vorannuhl stone is still missing; it lies in the deepest hall, reached by boat near Noota Nara. After that I dive from Bell Station off Lilmoth to the Teku-Sul gate.

Several questions are still open:
- What moans in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar, and where its key is.
- How Nesh-Deeka knows the Unbound.
- Why Cuts-the-Old-Knot seals the trees she drains. The tablet makes me suspect she wants the Eye lifted.

The game accepted my final notes and says it is over.
